The Negative Binomial Family

Source: R/family.R
negative_binomial.Rd

Specifies a negative binomial response for glgpm(), specify_glgpm() and maxim_integrand(), for counts that vary more than a Poisson model allows. A count \(y\) with exposure \(m\) given the random effects has mean \(\mu = m \exp(\eta)\), with the log link, and variance \(\mu + \mu^2 / \theta\), as in MASS::negative.binomial(theta). The size \(\theta\) is estimated unless a value is given, at which it is held.

Usage

negative_binomial(theta = NULL)

Arguments

theta

The size, a positive number at which it is held, or NULL (the default) to estimate it.

Value

An object of class riskmap_family_specification.

Details

The exposure is given in the denominator of glgpm(), and is 1 for every count when it is not given. As \(\theta\) grows the model tends to the Poisson model with the same mean, and a fit whose size goes to that limit holds it there, as a variance estimated as zero is held, and says so in check_fit(). A fit that estimates the size reports it in coef(), print() and summary() as theta. Its start is the size of the negative binomial regression without the random effects, or start_pars$theta in glgpm(). With one observation per location, an estimated size can't be told apart from a nugget or from a random effect with one level per observation, so those are refused. A fit with an estimated size uses the sampled form of Monte Carlo maximum likelihood (see integrate_noise in set_control_mcml()), and its check for other maxima has no screen of short scales. MASS::negative.binomial(theta) is read as negative_binomial(theta).

Given the size, the log-likelihood of a count is that of a binomial count of \(y\) successes in \(y + \theta\) trials with the logit link and the offset \(\log(m / \theta)\), plus terms in \(y\) and \(\theta\), which is how RiskMap fits it. The log-likelihood that a fit reports leaves out \(y \log m - \log y!\), as that of a Poisson fit does, so the two can be compared.

See also

glgpm(), stats::poisson()

Examples

negative_binomial()
#> The negative binomial family with the log link and its size estimated.
negative_binomial(theta = 2)
#> The negative binomial family with the log link and its size held at 2.
